formation.explanation: A proposal is buffered, forwarded, or appended by the role/phase owner. Leader prepare collects distinct per-pid promises for the configured read quorum, selects highest accepted round then length and maximum decided boundary, synchronizes that history, appends pending work, and sends AcceptSync. Subsequent accepted batches go to promised followers. Followers persist synchronized or appended history before Accepted; the leader counts per-pid indexes for a write quorum and persists/sends the decided boundary. Read APIs expose decided entries or the snapshot representation; application execution is separate.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds and manual attempts propose ballots, but SequencePaxos requires a ballot above its promise and former leader state. The new leader resets aggregation and persists its promise; a follower accepts higher Prepare, or same ballot only after recovery, flushing old buffered accepts before reporting its accepted history. A higher promise rejects old accepts and reports NotAccepted. Matching ballot plus phase and sequence/session checks protect follower append/decision processing; gaps trigger recovery. Crash recovery retains the promise/history but enters Recover and disables retaining leadership at the same own ballot.

connection.explanation: Authority acquisition does not discard prior accepted or decided history: promises carry accepted round/length and decision boundary; preparation selects history before accepting new proposals. AcceptSync transfers a suffix or a complete/delta decided snapshot, with session reset for later ordered accepts. Old-ballot replies cannot count in a new LeaderState. Same-ballot recovery re-promises and resynchronizes; existing accepted support refers to that ballot history. Buffered proposals survive preparation and are incorporated by a new leader or forwarded after follower sync unless a StopSign is present. Decided StopSign seals the configuration and caller starts new instances; configuration routing premises remain open. Snapshot content reconstruction is therefore a supporting storage responsibility directly consumed by A1 formation and A2 accepted-round transition.

grounding.derivation: Snapshot documentation describes compaction without discarding data and key-value create/merge semantics. The Storage SnapshotType contract defines Delta as changes since an earlier snapshot. The log contract guarantees decided entries are not reverted. Therefore after valid synchronization, the snapshot plus decided suffix must represent the same decided key-value prefix as the selected sender history; a delta must preserve earlier keys not overwritten by later entries. Existing snapshot tests independently compare snapshot contents to the input prefix. sync_log and its caller bind that requirement to actual history installation, not just index equality.
grounding.applicability: Valid fixed three-node configuration, correct key-value Snapshot implementation, fault-free MemoryStorage, generated FIFO messages with temporary partition and reconnect, no concurrent calls, no log trimming or reconfiguration.
alternatives: Complete snapshot replacement bypasses the delta merge; not the selected input.
